page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 4.5 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The processor includes 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor, provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier. Memory performance is strong, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 109.04 GB/sec. Multi-core performance and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 54.9 million operations per second, sit in the average tier. Small-model LLM inference performs in the top 10%, while medium-model inference speeds are average.

The r8a.4xlarge offers high memory density and strong single-core execution, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local storage. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy operations. The instance is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database caching layers, static web serving, and small-scale LLM inference tasks.
